mstts:express-as.prosody: Welcome—I'm so glad you're here. Have you ever wondered why some of the greatest civilizations in history soared to incredible heights, only to vanish as if they'd never existed? Together, we're about to embark on a fascinating journey—one that explores the hopes, ambitions, and hard lessons of the societies that came before us. Ronald Wright’s A Short History of Progress invites us to step into the footprints of Sumer, Rome, and Easter Island, and to reflect on the cycles that shaped—and sometimes shattered—them. We'll see how the pursuit of progress can spark remarkable achievements, but also how that same drive can push cultures to ignore the warning signs right in front of them. These echoes of lost empires aren’t just stories—they’re gentle reminders, urging us to look at our own choices and the world we’re building together. As we move through the ruins of the past, we’ll discover not only what made these societies thrive, but also what led to their downfall. And here’s the real question: what can we learn from their journeys to help guide our own? So, let’s dive in and explore the wisdom, the warnings, and the possibilities that come from understanding humanity’s shared path. This isn’t just history—it’s a chance for us to imagine a different future, together.
